full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana J. This Civil Petition for leave to appeal has been directed against the judgment and decree dated 30.11/008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1047 of 2007 discharging the Rule. 

 5. Against that judgment of the trial court the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No. 355 of 2005 in the court of the District Judge, Comilla and that appeal was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional; District Judge, Comilla. The appellate court below, on consideration of the evidence and the facts and circumstances found that the defendant executed the kabala deed in question on receipt of consideration of Tk. 25,000/- from the plaintiff and therefore, allowed the appeal, setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court and decreeing the suit of the plaintiff. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the appellate court the defendant filed the above mentioned revisional application before the High Court Division and the High Court Division, on hearing both the parties, upheld the judgment Of the appellate court making observation to the effect that in this suit since the defendant admitted his signatures on the disputed kabala the onus was upon him to prove the circumstances under which he put those signatures and that the defendant having failed to discharge that onus the appellate court rightly decreed the suit for specific performance of contract. 

 8. Mr. Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate appeared for the petitioner and has argued that the trial court, on consideration of facts, circumstances and evidence, rightly found that the plaintiff created kabala in question collusively beyond the knowledge of the defendant and without paying any consideration to the defendant and that subsequently the plaintiff without obtaining any order from the court got that kabala registered by practicing fraud upon the court; that the appellate court without reversing this clear finding of the trial court which had advantage of seeing the demeanor of the witnesses-decreed the suit most illegally. The learned Advocate has argued that the revisional court also without going into the evidence on record and considering the findings and decisions of the trial court upheld that the judgment of the appellate court which cannot be sustained. That the High Court Division did not at all consider the evidence adduced from the side of the defendant No. 1 before the trial court and thus arrived at a wrong decision which requires interference by this Division. 

 13. It has also been argued from the side of the petitioner that the plaintiff-respondent has got this disputed kabala registered without obtaining any order from court and thus the plaintiff has practiced fraud upon not only the defendant No. 1 but also upon the court. But this argument also of the petitioner is not acceptable at all. The he High Court Division, in its judgment, has made it clear that the suit for specific performance of contract was once decreed ex-parte and that decree was put into execution and as per the order of the executing court the deed in question was registered and after setting aside of the ex-parte decree, there was no application from the side of the defendant for cancellation of this registered deed in question.
